prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / stylized-concept.
Asset type: character orthographic MULTIVIEW DESIGN SHEET for the selected RuneNexus heavy tank guardian, based on the attached approved proposal 01.
Primary request: create ONE large high-resolution landscape character model sheet with FIVE clearly separated views of EXACTLY THE SAME CHARACTER: FRONT, SIDE, BACK, TOP, 3/4. Preserve the selected design faithfully rather than redesigning it.

Reference image is an IDENTITY AND MATERIAL reference, not a composition reference. Ignore the reference's small inset and its "01" number in your output. Closely replicate the MAIN character's shapes, proportions, colors and material appearance.
Identity invariants: one huge squat gray stone head, stern two glowing turquoise eyes under a very thick worn ochre-brass brow helmet. A broad central ochre-brass forehead/crown plate with ONE recessed turquoise angular spiral rune on its forward/upward surface. Gray stone top/rear of head remains partly exposed. Two massive rounded/chamfered ochre-brass shoulder shells wider than head, each shell split by the same broad dark gap seen in reference; no extra spikes. Small broad gray stone torso with exactly ONE small round amber glowing core inside a dark brass rim at front chest. Two arms: gray stone upper arm, dark recessed cylindrical elbow hinge, broad brass forearm armor cuff, chunky gray stone fists. Two legs: short heavy gray stone thighs, knees and shins with dark cylindrical hinge joints and small brass metal rims at ankle, large wide flat gray stone feet with the reference's simple toe splits. Dense low center of gravity, short limbs, broad upper silhouette, head about one third full height. No decorative belts or weapons.
Materials: weathered gray-brown stone with broad bevels, tiny fractures and fine granular natural texture; warm muted ochre-gold/brass armor with the original rough mottled patina and thick bevels, no glossy chrome. Dark charcoal joint cavities. Turquoise eyes and a single helmet rune, exactly one amber chest core; controlled glow.

Multiview consistency is CRITICAL. Think as if you built ONE 3D model and rotated its camera; all views must use the same neutral relaxed pose with arms lowered, closed fists, feet slightly apart, identical head/body size, shoulder-shell thickness and seams, same armor count, same joint positions and same foot shapes. Front and back centered, side shows a TRUE 90 degree profile looking LEFT, top shows a TRUE vertical bird's-eye orthographic projection with the character facing down the sheet. Show genuine overhead geometry, not an elevated front view. All parts rotate coherently and appear only when physically visible: eyes and chest core NOT visible on the back or true top; do not copy front face/core/rune onto rear head or back torso. Back is exposed broad gray stone head and compact stone torso, shoulder shells wrapping over rear upper arms and forearm cuff continuation only. Use modest consistent plain stone rear surfaces to complete unseen parts; do not introduce backpack, glowing back core, exhaust, additional runes, extra helmet crest, new giant back armor or new silhouette. Top exposes the original helmet's crown/forward central plate, gray rear head, BOTH gold shoulder shells and arm/foot placement. Shoulder seam layout must correspond in all views.

Layout: polished restrained landscape production sheet, roomy 3-column grid with FRONT SIDE BACK across the top row, TOP in lower left and a large 3/4 view spanning the remaining lower space. Front/side/back orthographic elevations have IDENTICAL character height, head top alignment and foot baseline. Top orthographic view uses the same world-unit scale for width and depth as the elevation widths/depths. 3/4 view is a matching physical design, may be slightly larger only for material readability. Each view fully visible with comfortable separation and at least 6 percent exterior margins; no overlap or cropping. Plain desaturated dark navy-gray background, no scenery, no platforms, no extra inset views. Soft even studio lighting reveals all faces, retain stone texture and armor thickness, very faint grounding shadows only. Sharp sculpted game-ready form readability and clean edges.
Text: only small restrained labels beneath corresponding views, verbatim "FRONT", "SIDE", "BACK", "TOP", "3/4". No headline, numbers, dimension rulers, annotations, watermark or logo.
Avoid: changing proportions between views, one view's gold shoulders becoming stone, humanoid knight redesign, giant boss proportions, whole body gold armor, weapons, shields held in hands, mirror-front used as back, heavy atmospheric lighting, cinematic poses, texture-only flat armor.
